PullRequest.Title: startup: Cache packaged ESM ASAR resolutions
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

- cache successful packaged ESM resolutions into `node_modules.asar`
- key entries by specifier, normalized parent path, conditions, and import attributes
- preserve closer-dependency precedence on the first resolution and avoid caching defaults or failures
- add a packaged ASAR integration fixture that verifies hits are reused but isolated by parent

The cache is process-local and lives for the process lifetime, so it also helps repeated dynamic imports after startup. CommonJS, built-ins, Electron modules, external extension paths, closer dependencies, and failed resolutions are unchanged.

## Performance

The motivating main-process trace found 33 ASAR resolution attempts from `out/main.js` for seven unique specifier-parent pairs, including 15 resolutions of `@vscode/spdlog` and eight of `@vscode/policy-watcher`.

### Packaged resolver benchmark

40 alternating baseline/cached Electron runs, excluding five warmups, shaped as 33 import sites over seven unique contexts:

| Metric | Baseline | Cached | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Resolution workload median | 44.184 ms | 19.172 ms | **-25.012 ms / -56.61%** |
| Electron process median | 135.250 ms | 109.649 ms | **-25.601 ms / -18.93%** |
| Archive lookups | 33 | 7 | **-78.79%** |

### Main-process CPU profiles

Six packaged launches per variant, excluding one warmup:

| Metric | Baseline | Cached | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Active main CPU median | 378.879 ms | 360.334 ms | **-18.545 ms / -4.89%** |
| Attributed JavaScript median | 366.230 ms | 347.248 ms | **-18.982 ms / -5.18%** |
| `internalModuleStat` median | 12.605 ms | 4.880 ms | **-61.29%** |
| Profiled elapsed median | 1,926 ms | 1,892 ms | -1.77% |

The profiler adds roughly 33-35% overhead in this local Code OSS package, so the CPU deltas are more reliable than the profiled wall-time delta.

### Full packaged startup

Ten unprofiled launches per variant, excluding one warmup:

- warm median: 1,422 ms -> 1,418 ms (**-4 ms / -0.28%**)
- warm mean: 1,425.67 ms -> 1,408.67 ms (**-1.19%**)
- run CV: 1.89% baseline, 1.55% cached

The median wall-time change is below run variance, so this PR does **not** claim a statistically significant end-to-end startup improvement. The demonstrated benefit is reduced resolver and main-process CPU, including for later repeated imports.

For the full-package A/B, the baseline forced the generated cache lookup to miss while retaining the small key/map overhead; every other application byte was identical. The standalone resolver benchmark compares the exact pre-change and changed bootstrap revisions.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`
- targeted ESLint
- focused bootstrap ESM tests: 6 passing
- full `vscode-win32-x64-min` package build
- packaged Code OSS startup A/B
- `git diff --check`

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Repeated imports of the same packaged bare module synchronously repeated default resolution and ASAR package/direct resolution instead of reusing the prior successful result.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Repeated synchronous module and ASAR resolution consumed main-process CPU during packaged startup and later repeated dynamic imports.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The hook keys successful archive resolutions by specifier, normalized parent path, conditions, and import attributes, then returns the cached resolver output before invoking the default resolver or ASAR lookup. It leaves failures, closer dependencies, external parents, CommonJS, and non-packaged processes uncached.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: Before this PR, every packaged ESM bare-specifier resolution that missed the default resolver reached synchronous ASAR resolution (`asarRequire.resolve`) even when the same specifier and parent had already resolved. The added integration test invokes four resolutions for two effective specifier-parent contexts and proves the changed hook performs only two archive package lookups plus two cache hits; without the added cache lookup/set, all four invocations follow the old archive-resolution path. `bootstrap-esm.ts` is imported by packaged Electron main/fork/CLI entry points, placing this repeated synchronous resolver work on startup and later dynamic-import paths.

Scenarios.Scenario: Packaged Electron startup and repeated dynamic imports of dependencies stored in node_modules.asar
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each synchronous resolve hook must finish before Node can evaluate the requested module, so default and archive resolution are on startup/import latency; cache-map work is also on this path but replaces resolver work on warm repeats.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Node default package resolution, ASAR package.json lookup, package self-reference resolution, and direct ASAR resolution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Cold: once per unique effective `(specifier, normalized parent path, conditions, import attributes)` context that reaches the archive, with direct fallback only for packages lacking self-reference support. Warm: zero resolver/archive calls for a cached successful context. The added test's four attempts across two parent contexts produce two archive lookups and two hits.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Every repeated successful archive resolution reran default resolution and the ASAR lookup; there was no process-local successful-resolution cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These synchronous operations block module evaluation and therefore packaged startup or the initiating dynamic import.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost now scales with unique successful import contexts rather than all attempts. Repeats of the same context are coalesced by the process-local map; parent isolation intentionally prevents sharing across distinct importing modules.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The synchronous registerHooks resolver handles attempts serially. Promise.all at callers can initiate multiple imports, but it does not parallelize the synchronous default/ASAR resolution work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The first successful archive resolution is cold and stored; identical warm contexts hit. Defaults, failures, CommonJS, built-ins, external parents, and non-packaged runs are not cached. Conditions and sorted import attributes are part of the key.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed-line control flow bypasses all resolver boundaries on a hit, and the test observes two hits replacing two archive lookups.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact startup savings vary by process/module graph, but the synchronous repeated-work mechanism and two-context/four-attempt reduction are directly established by the changed hook and integration test.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The small key serialization/allocation on each eligible attempt is bounded and is offset by eliminating synchronous resolver/archive work on repeated successful contexts; this PR fixes a concrete repeated-work regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Packaged imports that resolve to a closer dependency, fail, or differ by conditions/import attributes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Default resolution and any archive fallback must complete before the import can proceed or reject. Key construction is synchronous but contains only the specifier, parent path, conditions, and typically empty/small attributes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Default Node resolution for a dependency closer to the importer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call per attempt before and after the diff; successful default results are deliberately not cached by this map.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The hook performed the same default resolution once per attempt without first constructing a cache key.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: ASAR package.json lookup after default resolution fails or escapes the application.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One lookup per failed attempt and one per cold successful key; failures remain uncached. Distinct conditions or attributes remain distinct cold keys.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same lookup occurred for every such attempt, including repeats.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Added CPU/allocation scales with eligible bare-import attempts; retained entries scale only with unique successful archive tuples. Normal app and built-in-extension module graphs provide finite parent/specifier combinations, and repository searches did not establish a realistic unbounded successful-specifier source.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Resolution remains synchronous and serialized by Node's hook chain; the diff adds no concurrency burst or queued work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Closer/default resolutions and failures do not populate the cache. Different conditions and import attributes cannot collide; repeated failures retain no entries and repeat the pre-existing boundary work.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for control flow and cardinality; no evidence supports a user-visible regression from the bounded key allocation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact number of closer-dependency and failed attempts varies, but the added per-attempt key construction is small relative to synchronous resolver boundaries and no hot high-cardinality failure loop was found.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff adds minor serialization/allocation but does not increase filesystem boundary cardinality, and its process-lifetime retention is limited to successful unique contexts.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: Fixture filesystem setup completes in suiteSetup, then each added child Electron process must exit before its assertion runs; this affects only the targeted test suite, not product startup.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create a temporary packaged app, copy bootstrap outputs, write fixture modules, and build one ASAR archive.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Fixed suite-level setup: one temporary fixture and one archive, shared by both added tests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The suite created only the smaller reentrant-hook fixture.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds bounded setup latency to this test suite only.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Launch Electron-as-Node to exercise cache reuse and key isolation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly two additional child processes per suite execution, one per added test.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These two packaged-cache subprocess runs did not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each test waits for its child process; no product runtime path is affected.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: All added test work has constant fixture and subprocess cardinality; it does not scale with workspace, user data, or module graph size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Fixture copies/writes are grouped in one Promise.all where independent; the two new tests execute under the test runner's normal suite scheduling and each starts one child process.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Each child has a fresh process-local cache. The first test exercises two cold contexts followed by two warm hits; the second verifies two distinct cold keys.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High from the changed test setup and two explicit execFile calls.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Machine-dependent test duration is not measured, but cardinality is fixed and limited to a targeted bootstrap suite.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable product performance regression; the bounded test-only I/O and subprocess cost directly validates the optimization.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over both changed files and all hunks. Traced packaged startup, repeated imports, closer/default/failure paths, cache lifetime/key allocation, hook serialization, and test-only filesystem/subprocess boundaries. Submitted no findings because no actionable diff-introduced performance regression was established; recorded the verified repeated-resolution regression fix against its introducing commit.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
